sections.heading: The Pro2 is for a driver who actually wants rear-drive short course.
paragraphs: The Method Race Wheels 70021 Pro2 SC10 is a complete 1/10 brushless 2WD short-course truck. It is a useful choice for casual off-road practice and an organized class that accepts the package. The 322mm wheelbase and full short-course body create a different vehicle job from a smaller mini. I would choose it to learn the rear-drive format, not simply because Team Associated has a race history. Current 70041 SC10SW listings are separate purchases; the exact Method 70021 is the car assessed and linked here.

sections.heading: RTR leaves the battery, charger and radio cells to you.
paragraphs: The standard Method 70021 includes the assembled truck and installed electronics but needs drive power, a matching charger and four AA transmitter cells. The official completion information identifies NiMH or 2S–3S LiPo with a high-current T-plug. Select according to the exact manual and the available track space. The official press-release link label contains a 72021 typo, while its document filename and model contents establish 70021. That discrepancy is recorded instead of rewriting the identity.

The voltage options describe compatibility, rather than a requirement to begin with 3S. Resolve the driving area, pack fit and controller setup before choosing power equipment. The standard truck is also a different budget from a Combo: price the required battery and charger together before judging the car-only figure.

sections.heading: The rear differential and slipper do different jobs.
paragraphs: The Reedy 3300kV brushless system drives a rear gear differential through the 2.6:1 gearbox. The externally adjustable V2 slipper provides a separate means of managing drivetrain load, while the differential permits different rear wheel speeds. Treating both adjustments as one traction knob hides their different roles. Start with the manual's factory settings and a suitable initial power level. If a driving problem appears, inspect gear mesh and free drivetrain movement before buying a stronger motor or tightening every adjustment in the hope of improving it.

Choosing the Pro2 means choosing the rear-drive short-course format. A buyer mainly seeking a large-tire 4WD outdoor truck should weigh the Rival MT10 comparison before planning power upgrades. More motor output would not turn the Pro2's drivetrain and body format into the alternative vehicle.

sections.heading: DVC is assistance to understand, especially before a race.
paragraphs: The official Pro2 features include a Dynamic Vehicle Control receiver with an adjustable built-in gyro. That is part of the documented Method package, unlike assuming DVC from another Associated model's radio manual. Assistance still needs correct steering direction and sensible travel. A track can restrict electronic assistance, so check its rules before entering. Tim Mohr's Big Squid RC Method announcement is attributable exact-product coverage, not our driving test. We rate the equipment and setup opportunity rather than claiming that the gyro improves a measured lap time.

sections.heading: The stock geometry offers a meaningful learning path.
paragraphs: Steel turnbuckles, roll-center positions and 12mm aluminum big-bore oil shocks allow the owner to work with a recognizable race-truck suspension. Rear CVA shafts are documented factory equipment. These features make setup possible; they do not tell a new driver which tire, spring or geometry setting belongs at a specific track. Keep the factory values saved, inspect smooth movement and change one variable at a time. A driver learning rear-drive throttle control can benefit more from consistent practice than from adding every available Factory Team part.

sections.heading: The big shell does not make it a general-purpose monster truck.
paragraphs: The multi-terrain short-course tires and Method wheels belong to an off-road truck intended to cover suitable dirt surfaces and track obstacles. The 538mm overall length and 282mm width deserve usable course space. Thick grass or a rough improvised area can be a different proposition from prepared dirt. Begin with clear sightlines, sensible jumps and an open run-out. We have no measured tire-grip or jump comparison. If a club controls its tires, check that requirement before adding more tread or a different wheel offset to the purchase.

Measure the regular running area as well as the storage space. A short-course body can appeal even when the available ground is unsuitable; confirming the course first prevents the tire and suspension budget from becoming an attempt to solve that original mismatch. A mandated club tire should be priced before the first visit.

sections.heading: Method livery is finished, and the chassis remains accessible.
paragraphs: The factory body removes the trimming and painting work associated with a clear shell. Its enclosed receiver box and low molded chassis are practical ownership details, while the printed short-course presentation is a reason to select this variant. Removing the shell exposes the rear motor and battery layout for regular inspection. Keep the body mounts straight and the battery straps secure. We do not infer impact resistance from a large bumper or a water-resistant component description. Follow the exact 5-series RTR instructions for maintenance and part identification.

sections.heading: The $339.99 reference must be completed honestly.
paragraphs: The official Method standard RTR reference recorded on October 13, 2026 was $339.99. Add a compatible battery, charger and four AA cells with actual prices from your chosen supplier. An existing suitable pack is useful only if its chemistry, voltage, connector and physical fit match. Tools and routine cleaning equipment also matter, but their costs are not verified here and do not become a made-up subtotal. I would compare the full standard purchase with the LiPo Combo before ordering, then keep optional performance parts outside the initial essential basket.

sections.heading: The Rival MT10 changes the format and drivetrain.
paragraphs: Team Associated's Rival MT10 V2 20518 is a complete 1/10 brushless 4WD monster truck with larger all-terrain tires and independent suspension. It is worth considering when casual outdoor bashing matters more than rear-drive short-course practice or class preparation. Both standard RTRs need separate power equipment, so compare real completed baskets. Choose the Pro2 for the short-course body and the 2WD learning route; choose the Rival when its larger tire and 4WD format match the area. No lap-time, grip or durability winner is claimed.

The most useful comparison is the activity available each week. A nearby short-course group can give the Pro2's adjustment resources a clear purpose. If the regular activity is open-area truck play, the Rival's format may be the more relevant starting point. Complete each startup basket with its excluded equipment before comparing cost.
